item.title: Gunfire erupts between JSS, UPDF in Sajek
item.description:
Fresh fighting between armed members of two rival regional groups broke out in Sajek, Rangamati, on Saturday, heightening tensions in an area already reeling from weeks of violence, road blockades and the suspension of tourism.
Members of the Parbatya Chottogram Jana Samhati Samiti (JSS) and the United People’s Democratic Front (UPDF) exchanged gunfire in the remote Kalabunia area of Baghaichhari upazila from around 1pm, reportedly over control of the territory.
The shooting continued intermittently for nearly two hours, spreading panic among local residents.
No casualties had been confirmed as of the latest reports.
Sajek police station Officer-in-Charge Tofazzal Hossain confirmed the incident, saying the difficult terrain had prevented police from immediately reaching the site.
He said police and joint security forces were preparing to enter the area to bring the situation under control.
Security personnel were monitoring developments from a distance as tensions persisted.
The latest confrontation comes amid a prolonged dispute involving the JSS, led by Santu Larma, and the UPDF, led by Prasit Bikash Khisa, over territorial influence in Sajek.
The area has witnessed repeated incidents of armed violence in recent weeks.
On September 29, a nine-year-old girl, Sanjita Tripura, was wounded by gunfire during a clash between the rival groups in Sajek’s Chailyatali area.
Tensions escalated further in October when local organisations launched road blockades demanding action against armed groups.
On October 22, gunfire broke out between security forces and an armed group during an operation to escort tourists out of Sajek.
The Rangamati district administration subsequently suspended tourism in Sajek Valley until further notice, citing security concerns.
Repeated blockades have disrupted transport, restricted the movement of residents and affected the supply of essential goods.
Local organisations announced a 12-hour relaxation of the blockade for Sunday, but the latest exchange of gunfire has added to concerns over security in the region.
Police had not confirmed whether the fighting had ended or whether anyone had been injured.

item.title: Suspect arrested over extortion threats in Chittagong
item.description:
Alleged extortion threats against businessmen in Chittagong have led to the arrest of a man in Narayanganj, following claims that he demanded money over phone calls and threatened attacks for non-payment.
Sabbir Hossain alias Sunny was arrested during a police operation in Narayanganj on Friday night over the allegations. He allegedly targeted businessmen in the city's Panchlaish area.
During one such call, Sabbir said: “Contact your brother. You will contact him within 1 o’clock, all right? If I have to send boys and make something happen even once, the amount will become Tk 50 lakh or Tk 1 crore. It will not be reduced.”
According to police, Sabbir is an associate of Sazzad Ali alias Boro Sazzad, a top criminal from Chittagong who is currently a fugitive abroad. Although his home is in Satkhira, he has been living in the Hamjarbag area of Chittagong city for a long time.
Police sources said that last August, Sabbir called Mohammad Shawkat, the son of expatriate Mohammad Yusuf, a resident of Hamjarbag, and demanded extortion money. Shawkat is also an expatriate businessman.
During the phone call, Sabbir threatened to harm Shawkat's family members and said: “Contact your brother. Talk to him. Contact his Qatar number and settle the matter. If you do not settle it, we will first turn any one member of your family into a hornet's nest and start playing. Then, gradually, we will come after you. I did not call your father. He is a heart patient, and he might die or something. That is why I informed you.”
Police said they have an audio recording of the phone conversation. Following the extortion threats, shots were also fired at the gate of Yusuf's building.
Since then, police had been trying to arrest Sabbir, but he had been in hiding.
Speaking to reporters on Saturday afternoon, Chittagong Superintendent of Police Masud Alam said: “During interrogation, it was learnt that Sabbir received a monthly salary of Tk 50,000 from Boro Sazzad. He was also assigned the responsibility of carrying out extortion and other criminal activities in place of David Imon, who is in prison. Sabbir demanded extortion money over mobile phone calls under the instructions of Boro Sazzad and his associate Borhan Uddin.”
The superintendent of police further said: “Sabbir rarely appeared in public. His job was to call and demand extortion money according to the instructions of Sazzad and Borhan. Detailed information about the businessmen or industrialists from whom extortion money was demanded was collected beforehand. Police have information that Boro Sazzad collected this information through another group. Sabbir would then call and set a deadline for paying the money. If the money was not paid, he would threaten to send people to carry out attacks or open fire. Armed attacks were also carried out in accordance with these threats.”
Masud Alam said: “The arrested Sabbir has 2 cases against him at Panchlaish and Hathazari police stations in Chittagong. Although he demanded extortion money, most victims did not file cases out of fear.”
Police sources said that on June 20, Sabbir was seen brandishing a firearm and firing shots in the Kalurghat Industrial Area in the Chandgaon area of the city.
The incident was captured in a 37-second CCTV footage that circulated on social media platform Facebook. The footage shows a man wearing a T-shirt standing on the road and firing blank shots towards a factory. Later, as he walks along the road, he is seen raising his pistol and firing again.
Police identified the man in the footage as Sabbir.

item.title: Garment workers block roads in Mirpur
item.description:
Garment workers blocked roads at several points in Dhaka’s Mirpur area on Saturday to protest, disrupting traffic in the neighborhood.
The protests took place in Mirpur-10, Mirpur-11, Mirpur-12 and Proshika intersection.
The Traffic Mirpur Division of Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) said the demonstrations were disrupting vehicle movement in the areas. Police personnel were working to restore normal traffic conditions.
The division urged drivers and passengers traveling through the affected areas to allow extra time for their journeys and exercise caution.
Officer-in-Charge of Mirpur Model police station Hafizur Rahman said efforts were underway to restore normalcy through discussions with the workers.

item.title: Tahsif Sauri murder: Friend Shahriar Dip placed on 4-day remand
item.description:
A Dhaka court on Saturday placed Ahmed Shahriar Reza Dip, described as a younger friend of former Air Force official Tahsif Sauri, on a 4-day remand in a murder case filed over the recovery of Sauri’s body.
The order was passed by Dhaka Metropolitan Magistrate Hasib Ullah Piyas following an application submitted by the investigation officer, Inspector Firoz Uddin of the Tongi River Police Outpost.
Prosecution Department Sub-Inspector Saiful Islam confirmed the remand.
Inspector Firoz Uddin produced Dip before the court and sought a 7-day remand.
According to the remand application, preliminary investigations had found evidence suggesting Dip's involvement in the murder. The investigation is ongoing, and keeping him in custody until its completion is essential, the application stated.
The investigation officer sought remand on 5 grounds, including the possibility that Dip could flee if released on bail and hamper the investigation, the need to uncover the main mystery behind the case, and the need to arrest others involved in the murder.
Dip was produced before the court at around 2:15pm and kept in the detention room of the Chief Metropolitan Magistrate (CMM) Court in Dhaka. He was brought to the courtroom at around 3:25pm for the hearing.
State-appointed advocate Azizul Haque Didar argued in favor of the remand, while Monirul Islam and Mutasim Billah, representing Dip, sought its cancellation.
After hearing both sides, the court ordered a 4-day remand.
Earlier, the Police Bureau of Investigation (PBI) had taken Dip into custody for questioning from his residence in Mohammadpur on Thursday night.
As no case had been filed even after 3 days, discussions were underway about what decision would be taken regarding him. Amid this, he was handed over to the River Police on Friday night.
After Tahsif's father filed a case on Friday night, Dip was shown arrested.
Tahsif Sauri, who had been in the spotlight as the person who recorded the video of ousted prime minister Sheikh Hasina leaving the country, was found dead floating in the water.
River Police recovered his body from the Rajabari Ghat area of the Turag River on Wednesday afternoon.
He came downstairs at Dip's call on Tuesday evening and left home on his motorcycle.
Dip had said on Thursday that they had dinner together at a restaurant before he parted ways with Tahsif in the Uttara House Building area.
That night, the PBI took Dip into custody for questioning from his residence on Babar Road in Mohammadpur.
Based on information provided by him, Tahsif's motorcycle was recovered from the Mazar slum area of Tongi on Friday morning.
Dip also admitted to going with Tahsif to the area, which is known as a drug spot, around midnight. At one point, PBI officials also visited the area in Tongi with him on Friday.

item.title: Ex-DMP addl commissioner Harun dismissed from service
item.description:
Mohammad Harun-or-Rashid, former additional commissioner (Crime and Operations) of the Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP), has been dismissed from government service over prolonged unauthorized absence from his workplace.
The Home Ministry disclosed the decision in a notification issued on Saturday, stating that the dismissal would take effect retrospectively from August 6, 2024.
According to the notification, his unauthorized absence was treated as abandonment of service under government service regulations, prompting departmental proceedings against him.
Harun-or-Rashid, a deputy inspector general (DIG)-rank officer, was serving as additional commissioner (Crime and Operations) at the DMP when he stopped attending work without permission from the appropriate authority.
Despite repeated attempts to contact him at his current and permanent addresses and through email, he did not return to work.
Subsequently, Police Headquarters sent a letter to the Home Ministry requesting departmental action against him. A departmental case was filed on April 15 this year.
He was served with a show-cause notice seeking an explanation of the allegations but neither submitted a written response nor requested additional time.
An inquiry officer was appointed on June 22 to examine the allegations. The inquiry report, submitted on August 6, found the charge of abandonment of service established under Rule 3(c) of the Government Servants (Discipline and Appeal) Rules, 2018.
Harun was served with a second show-cause notice on August 20 but did not respond.
The government subsequently sought the opinion of the Bangladesh Public Service Commission (BPSC) on imposing the major penalty of dismissal from service.
In its opinion issued on October 1, the commission recommended his dismissal.
After reviewing the departmental case documents, inquiry report and BPSC opinion, the authorities found the allegations proven and decided to dismiss him from service, the notification stated.
The president approved the decision on October 25.
The order was issued by Senior Secretary of the Home Ministry Manzur Morshed Chowdhury on behalf of the president.

item.title: Ashulia garment workers protest for Tk30,000 minimum wage
item.description:
Workers from several garment factories staged protests in Ashulia, Dhaka, on Saturday, demanding a minimum monthly wage of Tk30,000, an end to blacklisting and other benefits.
Amid the unrest, at least 11 factories, including Nayem Knitwear Ltd., announced closures in the Kathgara area and surrounding neighbourhoods.
Ashulia Industrial Police-1 Superintendent Mohammad Mominul Islam Bhuiyan confirmed the matter around 11am.
He said a police officer was injured after being hit by bricks and stones thrown by protesting workers. The officer was taken to a hospital for treatment.
According to police, workers at Nayem Knitwear initially observed a work stoppage inside the factory in the morning. They later came out and began demonstrating.
At one point, the protesters threw bricks and stones at several nearby factories, triggering clashes and chases between the workers and police. The police officer was injured in the incident.
An official of a garment factory in the Kathgara Amtala area, speaking on condition of anonymity, said most factories in the area, except two or three, had declared holidays.
“We are monitoring the situation and will take further decisions based on the circumstances,” he said.

item.title: Bodies of 7 Bangladeshi workers killed in Riyadh fire arrive in Dhaka
item.description:
The bodies of 7 Bangladeshi workers killed in a fire at a sofa manufacturing factory in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, arrived at Hazrat Shahjalal International Airport in Dhaka at 8:30am on Saturday.
A total of 16 Bangladeshi workers died in the fire on August 9. The bodies of 9 workers were brought back to Bangladesh in the first phase on August 27.
The remaining 7 workers could not be identified initially as their bodies had been severely burned in the fire. Their identities were later confirmed through DNA tests.
According to embassy sources, all flights from Riyadh had been temporarily suspended since October 10. As a result, the bodies were transported by road from Riyadh to Jeddah.
They were then flown to Dhaka on a Biman Bangladesh Airlines flight from King Abdulaziz International Airport in Jeddah.
The 7 workers identified through DNA tests were Md Shahin of Sadar upazila in Naogaon; Md Hasibul Hasan Shuvo, Minhaj Pramanik, Md Masidul Sardar Sajib and Md Sagar Ali of Atrai upazila in Naogaon; and Mohammad Shamim and Md Sabbir Hossain of Naldanga upazila in Natore.

Saudi says intercepted ‘hostile drone’ in Riyadh region
item.description:
Saudi air defenses intercepted a drone in the Riyadh region on Saturday, according to the spokesman for the Saudi-led military coalition fighting Yemen’s Houthis.
“Air defenses intercepted and destroyed a hostile drone in the Riyadh region,” Turki al-Malki wrote on X, adding that “debris from the interception fell without causing injuries.”
Malki did not say who launched the drone.
In recent weeks, Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis have ramped up attacks on Saudi Arabia, including by launching deadly strikes on Riyadh airport that forced its closure for two weeks and the cancellation of flagship events -- threatening the kingdom’s economic diversification plans.
On Friday, Malki said the Houthis had targeted the Medina region, home to Islam’s second holiest city, but the group later denied the claim.
The Houthi attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure, airports and ships come after hostilities resumed in Yemen over the summer between the Houthis and the country’s internationally recognized government, which is backed by Riyadh.
More than 1,600 people have been killed and over 275,000 displaced since the fighting reignited, according to United Nations figures.
In July, a fragile 2022 truce fell apart after the Houthis allowed an Iranian plane to land in Yemen’s capital Sanaa in defiance of Saudi control over Yemeni airspace, setting off a spate of attacks.
Later, the Houthis declared a maritime blockade of Saudi Arabia and began hitting its ships, territory and oil facilities, before seizing Yemen’s entire Red Sea coast in a lightning campaign.
The Houthis have reported frequent Saudi airstrikes in areas they control as Riyadh retaliates.

Aarong plants 100,000 trees across Bangladesh
item.description:
Aarong, in partnership with Brac and Mission Green Bangladesh, has planted over 100,000 trees across 42 districts of Bangladesh as part of its Bring Your Own Bag (BYOB) campaign.
The initiative turns the proceeds of the campaign into environmental action while supporting rural households and expanding green spaces.
“Bring Your Own Bag began with a simple change in habit: carrying and reusing what we already have,” said Tamara Hasan Abed, managing director, Brac Enterprises.
“Today, those everyday choices are helping us plant trees, restore green spaces and create opportunities for communities across Bangladesh.”
Between September 2025 and March 2026, the BYOB campaign reduced paper bag consumption by over 4.68 million compared to the same period the previous year, equivalent to saving approximately 6,000 trees.
During this period, paper bag sales generated Tk2.9 crore, with Aarong committing the entire amount to tree planting and environmental restoration initiatives.
As part of this commitment, Aarong has funded the planting of 95,382 fruit, timber and medicinal saplings through Brac's Ultra-Poor Graduation program.
The saplings were distributed to 40,001 households across 210 upazilas in 42 districts, helping families improve household nutrition, develop potential sources of income and build long-term economic resilience.
Aarong has also partnered with Mission Green Bangladesh to establish Miyawaki forests, which use native tree species planted closely together to develop dense, biodiverse green spaces within relatively small areas.
At the Rupganj Miyawaki forest, Aarong brought together customers and members of the media to participate in a tree-planting drive, giving them an opportunity to contribute directly to the campaign they have supported.
Building on these efforts, Aarong welcomes partnerships with other organizations that share its interest in environmental restoration and community-led initiatives.
The BYOB campaign continues across all Aarong outlets, where customers receive a flat Tk15 cashback when they bring their own bags.
By connecting everyday shopping habits with environmental action, Aarong is extending its work beyond supporting rural artisans and preserving Bangladesh's crafts to creating greener communities for future generations.

item.title: Prab elects Yeahia Mirza president, Nazrul Islam general secretary
item.description:
Yeahia Mirza, head of PR and media at City Bank PLC, has been elected president of the Public Relations Association of Banks (Prab), while Nazrul Islam, head of public affairs and brand communication division at Dutch-Bangla Bank, has been elected general secretary.
The new leadership of the organization representing public relations officials of the country’s banks was announced on Thursday at a fellowship conference organized by Bonik Barta at a hotel in Gulshan in the capital.
Moniruzzaman Tipu, founding general secretary of Prab, declared the names of the new leadership.
Present on stage during the announcement were Prab founding president Ataur Rahman, outgoing president Shamsuddoha Shimu, and outgoing general secretary Jalal Ahmed Swapan, alongside senior members of the organization.
More than 200 officials working in the public relations departments of all scheduled banks and financial institutions in the country participated in the event.
Prab commenced its journey in 2011 with brand and communication officials from banks across the country.
The organization is typically administered by a 33-member executive committee formed for a two-year tenure.
Positions on this executive committee are held by public relations and branding heads of the country’s leading commercial banks, as well as high-ranking PR officials from Bangladesh Bank.
Regarding the formation of the full committee, Moniruzzaman Tipu said: “A 33-member executive committee will be formed through the Annual General Meeting (AGM) in coming November.”

item.title: Mahmudul Hoque new chairman of Jamuna Bank
item.description:
Md Mahmudul Hoque has been unanimously elected chairman of the board of directors of Jamuna Bank PLC.
The election took place at the bank's 486th board meeting on October 28, 2026.
Before assuming the role, Hoque served on the bank's board executive committee and previously served as the bank's chairman in 2012.
Hoque is one of Jamuna Bank's sponsor directors, and the bank said his unanimous election reflected the board's continued confidence in his leadership, understanding of the financial sector and experience in the country's industrial sector.
Hoque started his business career at a young age and has accumulated nearly 40 years of experience across textiles, power generation, banking, education and real estate.
In 1994, he founded Anlima Yarn Dyeing Limited, a publicly traded company listed on both stock exchanges in Bangladesh.
Several sister concerns of Anlima Group operate under his leadership.
Hoque is involved in corporate social responsibility and socioeconomic development initiatives within Anlima Group and through various social organizations and charitable causes. He has also travelled extensively internationally.
Born in Chittagong, Hoque is married to Hubbun Nahar Hoque, a sponsor shareholder of Jamuna Bank, and they have a daughter and a son, both of whom have established careers.

Mahdi Amin: Govt moves away from culture of artificially inflating pass rates, GPA-5
item.description:
Prime Minister's Adviser for Education and Primary & Mass Education Mahdi Amin on Saturday said the government has completely moved away from the old culture of artificially inflating pass rates or the number of GPA-5 achievers.
He said the Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) and equivalent examinations have now ensured a genuine and objective assessment of student merit.
Mahdi Amin announced that those who failed in one or two subjects will be given the opportunity to retake their examinations within one month.
In addition, he said, a comprehensive re-evaluation process for answer scripts - modeled after the system used for the SSC examinations - has been introduced.
The adviser made the remarks while speaking at a press conference held at the Ministry of Education's conference room in the Secretariat here.
Education and Primary & Mass Education Minister Dr ANM Ehsanul Hoque Milon officially unveiled the results at the press conference.
Regarding the overall examination environment and the assessment methodology, Mahdi Amin said that since assuming office, the incumbent government has taken a firm stance against the leaking of question papers.
By expanding the use of CCTV surveillance across examination centers, the exams were conducted in a highly positive and pleasant atmosphere, he said.
Addressing the evaluation of answer scripts, the adviser said, “Following the Prime Minister's directives, it has been ensured that the assessment of examination scripts is carried out with complete objectivity.”
“Moving away from the culture of artificially inflating GPA-5 scores or pass rates, the focus has shifted toward the genuine assessment of merit, maintaining the quality of question papers, and ensuring the integrity of the answer-script evaluation process,” he said.
To prevent the loss of an academic year for students, Mahdi Amin said measures are being taken to conduct re-examinations as quickly as possible - ideally within a month - so that students who have failed in one or two subjects do not lose a valuable academic year.
Congratulating the successful students, Mahdi Amin addressed parents and teachers, emphasizing that HSC results are not the ultimate benchmark in life.
He noted that fostering students' mental development and building their confidence is far more important than the results.
He said the government is taking an inter-ministerial, coordinated approach - extending beyond the traditional focus on producing doctors or engineers - to support the full development of each student's potential through modern technical education, vocational courses, and language training.
Gias Uddin Rimon, special assistant to the prime minister (Primary and Mass Education Ministry); Keramat Ali, acting secretary of the Secondary and Higher Education Division; as well as the chairmen of all education boards and senior ministry officials were present.

item.title: Spurned lover turns to drugs, sets up yaba factory
item.description:
Police have uncovered a yaba manufacturing facility inside a residential building in Tongi, Gazipur, and arrested a 32-year-old man in connection with the operation.
During the raid, police seized various equipment and chemical substances used to manufacture the drug.
The arrestee, Nazmul Islam Bappi, was detained around 1:30am on Saturday during a raid in the Pagar (Alectec) area of Tongi. He is the son of Taizul Islam and a resident of the same area.
According to police, Bappi had set up the facility himself after gathering information about yaba production from the internet, Facebook and YouTube.
Bappi claimed that he returned to Bangladesh several years ago after living abroad. He later became involved in a relationship with a young woman and turned to drug addiction after being emotionally distressed over the relationship. He subsequently decided to establish a yaba production facility.
Tongi East Police Station Officer-in-Charge Mohammad Maksudul Alam said police had been monitoring Bappi's residence for several days based on a tip-off.
Acting on the information, police raided the house late Friday night and discovered the facility on the fourth floor, along with a stockpile of chemicals and other materials used in yaba production.
The OC said the premises contained a laboratory and a concealed room built deep inside the building, making access difficult. Bappi had stockpiled various chemicals and other essential ingredients for manufacturing the drug.
During preliminary interrogation, Bappi admitted to collecting the chemicals to produce yaba, the OC added.

item.title: Dengue: One more dies, 1,633 hospitalized in 24 hours
item.description:
One dengue patient died in the last 24 hours till 8:00 am on Saturday while 1,633 were hospitalized after being infected with the mosquito-borne disease during the same period.
The latest fatality has raised the country's dengue death toll to 419 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the newly-hospitalized dengue patients, 604 were in Dhaka Division, 70 in Mymensingh Division, 281 in Chittagong Division, 228 in Khulna Division, 149 in Rajshahi Division, 67 in Rangpur Division and 234 in Barisal Division. According to the report, a total of 135,000 dengue patients have, so far, been hospitalized across the country this year.
So far, 128,345 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment in the hospitals.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the mosquito-borne disease last year.

item.title: West Indies crush Bangladesh by eight wickets in first Test
item.description:
Brandon King struck a career-best 81 not out as West Indies cruised to an eight-wicket win over Bangladesh in the first Test on Saturday to take a 1-0 lead in the two-match series.
King hit 10 fours and a six in his 115-ball knock to help the visitors chase down the target of 170 in 35.1 overs on the fourth day in Mirpur after Bangladesh were bowled out for 142 in their second innings.
Jomel Warrican, who was named player of the match, claimed 4-63 to follow up his five-wicket haul in Bangladesh's first innings as the hosts were bowled out in 48.4 overs.
West Indies captain Roston Chase took 5-36 in the second innings, his fifth five-wicket haul in Test cricket.
Bangladesh had resumed the fourth day at 79-6, holding a lead of 106, but their hopes of setting a challenging target suffered an early blow when Jaker Ali edged Warrican to slip, where Chase took the catch.
Jaker, who scored 22 off 34 balls, was the second-highest scorer for Bangladesh in the innings.
Nayeem Hasan survived two dropped catches off Chase, on 21 and 29, to keep Bangladesh going.
He added 26 runs with Hasan Mahmud before Warrican trapped the latter lbw for eight.
Taijul Islam contributed eight in a 17-run partnership with Nayeem before Chase dismissed him to leave Bangladesh at 127-9.
Nayeem then reached his maiden Test half-century off 87 balls, with four boundaries, but his resistance ended when he attempted to hit Chase over long-on and was caught by Joshua Bishop.
He made 52 off 91 balls, while Shoriful Islam remained unbeaten on seven as Bangladesh were dismissed cheaply.
West Indies started confidently, with openers King and John Campbell continuing their aggressive approach to take the visitors to 64 without loss in 14.1 overs before rain interrupted play.
After a delay of around an hour, they added another 23 runs before bad light and lightning forced a further stoppage of 45 minutes.
King was dropped on 70 by substitute fielder Ebadot Hossain off Taijul after the break, but the opener made Bangladesh pay with his fine, unbeaten knock.
Campbell fell just short of a half-century, bowled by Shoriful for 49 off 55 balls, with six fours and a six.
The second Test will be played in Sylhet from November 5.

item.title: Kane edged Mbappe in tightest Ballon d'Or vote
item.description:
Harry Kane won the Ballon d'Or by the smallest margin under its current voting system when he edged Kylian Mbappe by 28 points, France Football which runs the awards, revealed on Friday.
The magazine published a breakdown of the votes in its Friday edition.
Bayern Munich's Kane, the first Englishman to win the award since Michael Owen in 2001, received 40 first-place votes from the 100 jurors and a total of 1,055 points. France captain Mbappe of Real Madrid was placed first 23 times and finished with 1,027 points.
The previous smallest margin was 41 when Rodri, then of Manchester City, edged another Real player Vinicius Junior by 41 points in 2024.
Last season, Paris Saint-Germain forward Ousmane Dembele totalled 1,380 points as he finished 321 points ahead of Lamine Yamal of Barcelona.
This summer, Yamal won a World Cup with Spain but he finished third in the voting on 881 points, 174 behind Kane.
The Ballon d'Or is awarded following a vote by journalists (one per country) representing the top 100 nations in the FIFA rankings for men, and the top 50 for women.

item.title: India bolster pace attack for New Zealand ODIs
item.description:
India have bolstered their pace-bowling options ahead of their five-match ODI series against New Zealand, as the Men’s Selection Committee have added Auqib Nabi to India’s squad for the first three ODIs of the upcoming series.
Nabi was initially named in the unit for the fourth and fifth ODIs but will now be available from the beginning of the series, starting Wednesday, November 4.
The 29-year-old made his debut in last month's second ODI against the West Indies.
India have also retained the rest of their originally announced squad for the first three matches, with Nitish Kumar Reddy available only for the opening ODI.
Earlier, India had announced that Prasidh Krishna will sit out the ODI series after being unable to secure a fitness clearance.
The two sides are currently engaged in a five-match T20I series, where India have a unassailable 3-1 lead with the final T20I set for Sunday, November 1.

Nations commit to get nature goals back on track
item.description:
Nearly 200 nations struck hard-fought agreements Friday at a UN biodiversity summit, but the outcome was accompanied by disappointment over missed opportunities to address humanity’s destructive toll on nature.
Delegates cheered as crucial texts were approved in overtime but the celebrations were tempered by acrimonious debates and regret over limited progress on some of the most contentious issues.
The COP17 summit in Armenia sought to revive a landmark commitment to halt and reverse the destruction of nature by 2030 after global efforts to meet that goal fell short.
Over two bruising weeks in Yerevan, nations were urged to correct course to keep the pact alive and protect the plants, animals and ecosystems that sustain life on Earth.
The United Nations had warned that progress was insufficient to meet the goals of the 2030 target including protecting 30 percent of Earth’s land and oceans, tackling pollution and invasive species, and boosting money for conservation.
“And that’s it. Perfect,” said COP17 president Hambardzum Matevosyan in Armenia as he brought down the gavel on two major texts, the final versions of which were still not available early Saturday.
But the outcome was “not commensurate” with the crisis engulfing the natural world, said French Ecological Transition Minister Monique Barbut on Saturday.
“The progress we failed to achieve here is a series of missed opportunities to speed up our response to the loss of biodiversity,” Barbut said in a lengthy statement sent to AFP, stressing that “nature will not wait for the pace of our negotiations.”
The final plenary stretched through Friday night and well into the next morning, with negotiations turning sour as the hours dragged on.
Even as some delegates left to catch flights, others stayed behind to argue technical points.
Veteran COP observer Juliette Landry from the IDDRI think tank told AFP “there was a lot of push and pull in every direction” throughout the summit and “in that context, it’s hard to get things accepted.”
UN biodiversity chief Astrid Schomaker said the summit had achieved some “quite remarkable things at a moment when multilateralism is supposedly not functioning.”
“Some of these more difficult subjects, we could not expect to have strong negotiated commitments. That was never the plan,” she told reporters after the summit’s close.
In a draft agreement of one closely watched text, nations were urged to “accelerate” their efforts and warned that “increased action” was needed to tackle the forces driving biodiversity loss.
This “represents a positive outcome... and though there are weaknesses, particularly on harmful subsidies, it does represent a step forward,” Guido Broekhoven from WWF International told AFP.
Tackling subsidies and other incentives that encourage activities harmful to nature -- such as fossil fuels, intensive agriculture and overfishing -- was one of the most politically fraught agenda items at the summit.
“Even though the agreed decision text expresses it in weak terms, COP17 saw important political momentum to address harmful financial incentives, including subsidies,” An Lambrechts from Greenpeace International told AFP.
A rare fight over science cast a pall over the summit, with a number of countries accused of undermining efforts to approve key reports in scenes that shocked even seasoned negotiators.
“We regret the increasing instances in which scientific evidence and its uptake has been challenged or constrained” by politics, said Swiss negotiator Gabriela Blatter in a statement on behalf of dozens of countries.
“Our delegations fully respect every state’s right to safeguard national interest but science is not negotiable.”
A separate row revolved around finding new cash sources to fund conservation efforts -- another hot-button issue with public budgets under strain amid an energy crisis and conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East.
The European Union led a charge for wealthy emerging economies such as China to contribute to global conservation efforts, a contentious issue at COP17.
In a sign of possible compromise, another draft text that circulated Friday invited countries outside the developed-country donors to voluntarily join the group.
Outstanding questions over the design of the Cali Fund -- a UN mechanism that hoped to attract billions of dollars in corporate contributions but is close to empty -- were left unresolved.
“By punting essential decisions to two years from now, parties have all but ensured the fund remains empty until then,” said Pakhi Das from the nonprofit organization Plant-for-the-Planet.
The COP17 summit decided early Saturday that Ecuador would host the next biodiversity talks in 2028 after the South American nation defeated rival candidate Panama in a secret vote.

item.title: Bollywood and the underworld — together in the spotlight?
item.description:
“In the entire film industry, whoever works without aligning with us, or works with Salman Khan, will be killed.”
This warning was delivered in an audio message by presumed attackers on Indian actor Tiger Shroff in Mumbai earlier this month, as they claimed responsibility for the shooting.
The apparent perpetrators said they were connected to Lawrence Bishnoi, a student-politician-turned-gangster who has been in prison since 2014. Notably, police have not confirmed the gang’s involvement.
The shots fired at Shroff, which injured his driver, were only the latest in a string of attacks targeting prominent figures from the Mumbai-based film industry, popularly known as “Bollywood.”
Since 2022, gunmen fired shots at actor Salman Khan’s apartment and at the home of filmmaker Rohit Shetty in Mumbai, as well as actor Disha Patani’s family home in northern India. Actor Ranveer Singh also reportedly received an extortion demand of nearly $1.1 million.
The attacks have spread to the other side of the globe, with a cafe owned by comedian Kapil Sharma in Surrey, Canada, also hit three times.
For an industry that once lived in the shadow of organized crime, the attacks have revived old fears, harking back to the crime bosses of the 1990s. But experts say the threat facing Bollywood today looks very different from the one it faced three decades ago.
In the 1990s, Mumbai’s underworld was deeply entangled with the Hindi film industry.
“The mafia was always fascinated with the movie industry,” said S Hussain Zaidi, crime journalist and author of “Dongri to Dubai: Six Decades of the Mumbai Mafia,” who has covered organized crime in the city for over three decades.
Gangsters like Dawood Ibrahim, Abu Salem and Chhota Shakeel “were totally obsessed” with Bollywood, he told DW, much like mafiosi who sought a foothold in Hollywood.
To the gangsters, films offered glitz and glamor, but also a way to launder their profits. They invested in films “so that they could control the industry and have a legitimate way of making money,” Zaidi added.
When producers didn’t cooperate, the consequences could be fatal. In 1997, music mogul Gulshan Kumar, founder of the label T-Series, was shot dead. In 2000, filmmaker Rakesh Roshan, father of Bollywood star Hrithik Roshan, was shot and wounded.
Mumbai’s streets were “made red with blood” in 1998, Zaidi said, describing the year as the pinnacle of gang killings.
D Sivanandhan, the former Police Commissioner of Mumbai, who led the crackdown, says 101 businessmen were shot dead in 1998 alone, or one “every third day,” mostly over unpaid extortion demands.
Police efforts were reinforced by a tough new organized crime law passed in 1999, which Sivanandhan calls the “ultimate weapon.” Security forces used electronic surveillance and preventive detention, and seized some 2,500 illegal weapons.
“A few encounters also happened, but that is not a policy nor a strategy,” he told DW, referring to police shootouts.
By the early 2000s, the gangs’ hold had been broken, and a new Mumbai seemed to be emerging.
The man believed to be behind the latest wave of attacks is not from Mumbai.
Bishnoi, 33, comes from a landowning family in the northern state of Punjab and was studying in Chandigarh when he was drawn into violent student politics. Then, he was arrested, incarcerated and eventually turned to crime, says journalist Jupinderjit Singh, author of “Gangs of Punjab.”
“He was introduced to the University of Crime through the jail,” Singh told DW.
Bishnoi went on to build what Singh describes as one of the first criminal syndicates spanning several northern Indian states. Investigators say he still directs operations from prison using concealed phones and messaging apps.
Currently, Bishnoi is held in a jail in Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s home state of Gujarat.
His network stretches beyond India’s borders. In September 2025, Canada designated the Bishnoi gang a terrorist entity. Last month, the FBI added Satinderjeet Singh, popularly known as Goldy Brar, to its Ten Most Wanted list, offering up to $1 million for information leading to his arrest. US prosecutors described him as the alleged leader of Bishnoi’s group in North America.
While Bishnoi comes from an affluent landowning family, his shooters are mostly poor. The gang usually recruits them online.
“There are so many youngsters who want to do something… they are just pulled by the lore attached to Lawrence Bishnoi,” Singh explained. “Recruiting is no big issue… They offer money, protection, weapons.”
For Bishnoi, it seems personal.
In 1998, Salman Khan was accused of killing a blackbuck, an antelope revered by Bishnoi’s community. Bishnoi vowed revenge, and many of the attacks targeted people close to the actor, including the 2024 killing of politician Baba Siddique, which police have linked to the gang.
Singh sees the feud as a bid for respectability. Criminals “always try to find something that makes them a moral guardian,” he says, and this case was Bishnoi’s “chance to redeem himself.”
But money and intimidation matter too.
“Bollywood has a lot of money,” Singh added, pointing that the previous generation of gangsters was no longer in position to take advantage.
“With Dawood Ibrahim and his counterparts away, there was a vacuum, and Lawrence Bishnoi is trying to exploit that.”
Sivanandhan explained the old Mumbai gangs ran a whole “basket” of illegal businesses, from smuggling to protection rackets and cricket match-fixing. Their members were “local boys,” while the Bishnoi gang has “nothing to do with Mumbai,” he added. It targets Bollywood because the industry is “loaded with money” and a “soft underbelly.”
“They are using Bollywood as an ATM,” he told DW. “Insert a card and collect your money.”
Meanwhile, Zaidi sees the attacks mainly as publicity. “It’s a way to grab headlines,” he told DW. Within hours of the recent attack on Shroff, someone claimed on social media that he was targeted for being close to Khan, a logic Zaidi called “absolutely illogical and absurd.”
But publicity is useful to gangs that live off extortion. “The base material of extortion is: create fear,” a security professional responsible for the protection of several Bollywood stars, who asked not to be named because of the sensitivity of the issue, told DW.
Still, experts say its hard to argue that the ongoing violence is comparable to the 1990s crime wave.
“I won’t say resurgence, because that would be a bit of an exaggeration,” Zaidi said. In the 1990s, several rival gangs fought for control of Mumbai. Today, other than Bishnoi’s faction, other gangs are not considered active in Mumbai.
The film industry is also not paying up the way it once did, because the shift to digital payments has made large cash transactions hard to hide, he added.
Sivanandhan disagrees. The shootings at walls and gates, followed by quick claims on social media, are “all aimed at collecting… extortion money,” he said. In his view, “cash-rich Bollywood would be coughing up so much, which is enough to run an army of people.”
At any case, the fear remains real.
And even if violence is not as prevalent, hundreds of thousands of people rely on the Mumbai film industry for their livelihoods.
“If the fear of the underworld continues, leading names may be forced to leave Mumbai,” the All Indian Cine Workers Association (AICWA) President Suresh Shyamlal Gupta wrote to Home Minister Amit Shah.
“Mumbai will not be allowed to go back to the underworld days of the 1990s, and Bollywood will not be allowed to work in the shadow of fear,” Gupta wrote.
With security forces seemingly on the back foot, gangsters are likely to continue their campaign.
Several Bollywood stars have already stepped up their security.

item.title: Iran’s supreme leader warns US, Israel against new attacks
item.description:
Iran’s supreme leader Mojtaba Khamenei on Saturday warned the United States and Israel against returning to war, according to a written statement, following threats from the Islamic Republic’s foes of a possible resumption of strikes.
“If the enemies once again launch military or terrorist attacks, it is the armed forces of the Islamic Republic and the Iranian nation that will determine the time and conditions for ending them,” said a statement attributed to Khamenei posted on his website.
The remarks came during a reported meeting between Khamenei and senior military commanders, including armed forces chief of staff Ali Abdollahi, army chief Amir Hatami and Revolutionary Guards commander Ahmad Vahidi. It was the first reported meeting between them.
Khamenei has not been publicly seen since he became supreme leader, following his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei’s killing in US-Israeli strikes at the start of the Middle East war in February.
According to the statement, Khamenei ordered the commanders to ensure that “any level or type of threat must be met with an immediate, impactful and geographically unrestricted response.”
It also said that Khamenei ordered the commanders to update Iran’s target list to include “all types of tangible and intangible assets belonging to the American-Zionist enemy.”
The war began on February 28 with US-Israeli strikes on Iran, which swiftly responded with attacks on countries around the region.
The supreme leader’s statement came as fresh diplomatic efforts were underway to avert a resumption of fighting.
A Qatari delegation arrived in Tehran on Friday for talks with Iranian officials, after Iran reportedly received a letter from US Vice President JD Vance.
According to Iranian media, Tehran had yet to respond to the letter.

item.title: European diplomats shun Russia at G20 gathering in the US
item.description:
A Group of 20 foreign ministers’ meeting in the US city of Atlanta got off to a rocky start on Friday after top diplomats from European nations refused to take a “family photo” along with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is hosting the gathering, decided to scrap the photo before the meeting got underway because Washington didn’t want it to become a spectacle or distraction.
German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul told reporters before the first session on Friday that there wouldn’t “be a family photo with European partners and Mr. Lavrov together because ... there is no normalcy with Russia.”
The two-day gathering of the G20 grouping, which includes the EU, Russia, Germany, India, China, Brazil and other major countries, is meant to be a precursor to a G20 leaders summit later this December.
That G20 leaders meeting in December is set to be hosted by US President Donald Trump at his golf club in Miami.
Rubio still opened the talks by stressing unity on major issues, telling his counterparts that they were in a “critical moment.”
“We are facing a series of interconnected economic and geopolitical crises,” he said.
He pointed to disruptions to global energy and trade and said many were posing “severe threats to essential foundations of the global economic order.”
But several countries, including the United States and Russia, are involved in separate wars. Wars in Iran and Ukraine have resulted in a spike in food prices for people around the world.
While the message is about unity and finding solutions to problems like freedom of navigation in the Black Sea and the Strait of Hormuz during the G20 meeting, the reality is that finding common ground will likely be much tougher.
Given a renewed momentum to revive talks to end the war in Ukraine, there was also interest in getting Lavrov to talk about Russia’s stance on future talks with Kyiv.
The US has invited Russian President Vladimir Putin to the G20 meeting in Miami, but it’s unclear whether Russia has accepted the invitation.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has previously said that he would be open to traveling to Miami to hold talks with Putin if he were also there.
The Kremlin has so far declined direct meetings with Zelenskyy, with Russia’s Sergey Lavrov telling DW on the sidelines of the meeting that Putin is willing to meet with the Ukrainian leader if he travels to Moscow.
“President Putin said if he [Zelenskyy] is willing to meet, let him come to Moscow,” Lavrov said. “We will guarantee his safety.”
Lavrov declined to say whether Putin will attend the G20 summit this December.
Putin has not attended a G20 leaders meeting since 2019 and only attended a session virtually in 2023.
Russia has also continued with its attacks on Ukrainian cities in recent weeks, stepping up drone strikes on water and energy infrastructure.
The European Union’s top diplomat, Kaja Kallas, said ministers at the G20 meeting were able to call out Lavrov for his “lies” at the table.
“We were talking about the big geopolitical crises, including Ukraine, and we were able to address Sergey Lavrov head-on with this,” Kallas said on the sidelines of the meeting.
“Of course, he put forward a lot of lies, a lot of false narratives that we were also able to then rebuke,” she said.
British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband also called out Lavrov, saying, “If we are serious about our values and our interests, we must also work harder to secure just and lasting peace in Ukraine.”
Lavrov, who is under international sanctions for Russia’s war in Ukraine, was invited to the US at a time when the two countries have appeared to have fostered warmer ties.
Trump announced a diesel deal with Russia earlier this month and also waived new sanctions on Russia’s energy. The US announced the move just weeks away from the midterm elections on November 3.
Lavrov said on Friday that despite those efforts, “in practice, no real progress in relations with the US has so far been seen.”
The Trump administration has been embroiled in disputes with South Africa, having imposed visa restrictions on South Africans who it said were complicit in discriminating against white people.
Ukraine, which is not a G20 member but was invited to attend previous such meetings, was not invited this year because US officials said they made a conscious choice to include only formal members of the group.
But US officials didn’t extend that invite to South Africa, a G20 founding member and the only African country in the group.
“We have consistently maintained that our nonparticipation is not voluntary,” said Phindile Kunene, spokesperson for South African Foreign Minister Ronald Lamola.
With this many issues on the table, it appeared less likely that there would be a joint consensus at the end of the talks.
Instead of a final declaration, the AFP news agency reported, the meeting is expected to end on Saturday with a chair summary drafted by the US.

item.title: Mark Carney: Canada has ‘learned we are overdependent on the US’
item.description:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney spoke to DW on Friday after talks in Montreal with European Union leaders seeking to hammer out details of a new, closer partnership between Canada and the EU.
Amid difficult negotiations with US President Donald Trump, representing Canada’s biggest trading partner, Carney said that he and his compatriots had come to realize the country was too dependent on the economic powerhouse to the south.
“The lesson we’ve taken, Canadians as a whole, is we’re overdependent on the United States. Too closely connected to the United States. And we need to build our strength here at home and diversify and deepen our partnerships with like-minded countries internationally,” Carney said.
An EU delegation led by European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President Antonio Costa held talks with Carney and other Canadian officials in Montreal on Friday.
They’re discussing the plans floated by Commission President Ursula von der Leyen to forge what she called an “associate membership” — a status that does not yet exist for any other country — even as German Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s government resists creating this label. Carney seemed to speak in its favor.
“Well, I think the advantage of what we’re doing is that a few things are absolutely clear, irrespective of the exact terminology that’s used. President von der Leyen uses associated membership. We use associated membership,” he told DW’s Katharina Kroll at Port of Montreal Tower.
“What does that mean? It means the closest possible partnership without being a full member of the European Union, because Canada is not in Europe geographically and therefore cannot have accession.” Carney said.
Asked if he was looking to create a “new transatlantic bloc without the US,” Carney said it was more about diversifying and deepening Canada’s other partnerships than excluding by far its largest trading partner.
“We’re both partners of the United States, obviously close partners, alliance partners in Nato. And there are many, many opportunities for cooperation with the United States,” he said. “But in many cases, there’ll be much deeper cooperation for Canada between Canada and Europe than Canada and the United States.”
He mentioned both existing areas of cooperation like the Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (Ceta), calling it “one of the most successful free trade agreements in the world,” and also pointed to research cooperation and programs like Horizon Europe and Erasmus+ enabling student exchanges.
But Carney also pointed to areas where the two sides could seek to expand cooperation, naming areas like space technologies, artificial intelligence and critical minerals.
Despite his well-documented difficulties with Donald Trump — perhaps most crudely exemplified by Trump’s attempts to unilaterally rename Lake Ontario, or his posting AI videos imagining him as an ice hockey player beating Carney up in a fight — Carney said US-Canadian ties were too deep to be derailed by any governments or prime ministers or presidents.
“The bonds between Canadians and Americans are longstanding. They’re very strong. And big elements of that will be maintained regardless of the government in Canada, the government in the United States, the combination of the two,” he said.
Asked about the best way to deal with Trump, Carney said it was “to be direct, to be clear, to be absolutely clear about your bottom lines are.” He said it was important to show respect but also to continue to bring “the negotiations back to the core issues.”
But he said the tensions with Trump had demonstrated the need to diversify and to seek Canada’s other most natural partners around the world.
He acknowledged that no matter the nature of the talks with the EU, “the scale of the relationship with the United States” would be “very hard to replace.”
Asked if he was concerned that the talks could expose him to further tariffs or other punitive measures from the Trump administration, Carney said, “We’ve been living with this for some time.”
“There have been many justifications for trade action against Canada that the United States has had,” he said. “Our view is that all of them are unjustified under our trade agreement.”
Carney said the crucial message, also for the Trump White House, was that the talks with Brussels concerned a “positive association” and partnership “to help solve global problems” and address global challenges.
“It’s not against somebody. It’s for. It’s a positive act,” he said.

Rajshahi district leads board in pass rate, GPA-5
item.description:
Rajshahi district has topped the eight districts under the Rajshahi Education Board in both pass rate and the number of students securing GPA-5 in this year’s Higher Secondary Certificate (HSC) examinations.
Despite Rajshahi’s strong performance, the overall results of the board were disappointing, with the pass rate falling to 45.06% this year. More than half of the students who appeared for the examinations failed.
Girls, however, outperformed boys in both pass rate and GPA-5 achievements.
Only nine colleges across the eight districts recorded a 100% pass rate, while no student from 39 colleges passed.
Rajshahi Education Board Controller of Examinations Professor Iffat Zerin announced the results at 11:00am on Saturday.
According to the board, 4,520 students secured GPA-5 this year. Of them, 1,785 were from Rajshahi district, accounting for nearly 39.5% of all GPA-5 achievers under the board.
Bogra ranked second with 1,309 GPA-5 achievers, followed by Pabna with 550.
Rajshahi also recorded the highest pass rate at 55.33%. Bogra ranked second at 53.64%, while Joypurhat stood third at 41.67%.
A total of 141,936 students registered for this year’s HSC examinations under the Rajshahi Education Board. Of them, 137,356 appeared, with 61,894 passing and 75,462 failing.
In Rajshahi district, 28,086 students appeared for the examinations, of whom 15,540 passed.
Students from 743 colleges across the board’s eight districts took the examinations at 208 centres.
Girls recorded a pass rate of 53.03%, compared with 37.71% for boys. Of the 4,520 GPA-5 achievers, 2,555 were girls and 1,965 were boys.
Professor Iffat Zerin said 31 examinees were expelled for adopting unfair means during the examinations.
She said only nine colleges recorded a 100% pass rate, while 39 colleges had no students passing.

item.title: Heading to Saint Martin’s this week? Here’s how to reach the island
item.description:
Tourists flock to Saint Martin’s Island every year, drawn by its natural beauty. After a long wait, the country’s only coral island is set to reopen to tourists on November 1.
Although tourism activities will resume on the island, ships will not operate during the first five days. Ship services are scheduled to begin on November 6.
This naturally raises a question: how will tourists reach Saint Martin’s Island during these five days?
According to available information, tourists will have to rely on trawlers or speedboats to travel to the island during this period. This means that those planning to visit Saint Martin’s Island between November 1 and 5 will have to use these alternative watercraft.
However, travel by trawler or speedboat will depend heavily on weather conditions, the state of the sea, and permission from the relevant authorities.
This raises several questions. If tourists can travel to the island by trawlers or speedboats, then what is the need for regular ship services?
Travelling by ship may take comparatively longer and cost more. Yet ships hold a different kind of importance for tourists: safety and a relatively stable journey.
For sea travel, larger vessels are generally considered safer and more comfortable than trawlers or smaller speedboats. This is particularly important when the sea is rough, as travelling in smaller vessels can become risky.
So, why will ship services begin five days later?
One of the main reasons is that the vessels concerned have not yet received the necessary clearance from the Department of Environment.
Ship operations are expected to begin on November 6, once the required clearance and other formalities have been completed.
In other words, although the island will reopen to tourists, ship services cannot begin immediately because the approval process is still underway.
Regulating tourism has always been important for protecting the environment and biodiversity of Saint Martin’s Island.
Therefore, before planning a trip, tourists should check the approved modes of transportation, ship schedules, and the latest instructions from the relevant authorities.
Those planning to visit during the first five days should be particularly careful and confirm the safety of travelling by trawler or speedboat, check the weather forecast, and ensure that all necessary permissions are in place before setting out.
The doors to Saint Martin’s Island will reopen on November 1, but tourists will have to wait another five days for regular ship services.
So, before heading to the island, keep in mind not only the travel date but also the mode of transportation and safety arrangements.

item.title: Does charging your phone overnight damage the battery?
item.description:
For many people, putting the phone on charge before bed and unplugging it in the morning is a regular habit. But once the battery hits 100%, many wonder whether keeping it connected to power for hours on end causes damage. With modern smartphones, though, the matter is a little different.
Today’s smartphones usually use lithium-ion or lithium-polymer batteries. Once the phone is fully charged, its charging system reduces the current supplied as needed or shuts off the main charging process. So even after reaching 100%, power does not keep flowing into the battery in the same way. The idea that leaving a phone on charge overnight will “overcharge” and ruin it is therefore not correct.
Even without overcharging, keeping a battery at full charge for a long time is not ideal. In lithium-based batteries, holding a full charge for long periods can gradually speed up chemical degradation. Over time, this affects the battery’s maximum capacity.
As a result, after months or years of use, you may notice the phone’s charge running out faster than before. In other words, the biggest concern with charging overnight is not instant “overcharging,” but a somewhat faster decline in the battery’s health over the long term.
Temperature matters a great deal for batteries. While it is normal for a phone to get a little warm while charging, excessive heat can put extra stress on the battery.
In particular, you should not charge the phone under a pillow, blanket, or bedding. In such places, there is little airflow around the phone, so heat cannot escape easily. It is a safer habit to charge the phone on a hard, flat, open surface.
To help preserve battery life, many smartphones now come with special charging features. Depending on the phone, these may be called Optimized Charging, Adaptive Charging, or Battery Protection.
These features analyze the user’s charging habits and often avoid holding the phone at 100% for long, instead completing the full charge closer to a set time. This reduces the amount of time the battery spends fully charged.
So, is it fine to sleep with the phone on charge?
Because modern smartphones have multiple safeguards that control charging, leaving the phone plugged in overnight generally won’t cause immediate damage. However, to keep the battery healthy in the long run, it is best to avoid overheating and keep features such as Optimized Charging or Battery Protection enabled.
Remember, a smartphone battery is a consumable component. Even with good care, its capacity will decline over time. The idea that a battery is ruined only because of overnight charging is not correct. Rather, temperature, usage patterns, and the age of the battery all combine to determine how long it lasts.

item.title: Try these five tricks to stop overpaying for your AC
item.description:
As temperatures continue to rise, staying comfortable indoors has become increasingly difficult. From ceiling fans and air coolers to air conditioners, people are relying on different cooling solutions to cope with the heat. However, running an air conditioner for extended periods can raise concerns about electricity costs, particularly among middle-income households.
Many people limit their use of air conditioners at night to avoid high electricity bills, often compromising their comfort in the process. However, with a few adjustments to everyday habits, it is possible to maintain a comfortable indoor temperature while managing energy consumption.
Here are some practical ways to make your air conditioner more energy-efficient.
The temperature setting plays an important role in determining how much electricity an air conditioner consumes. Lower settings require the compressor to work harder and for longer periods, increasing energy use.
According to a recent study cited in the original report, each degree of reduction in the temperature setting can increase electricity consumption by around 6%. Keeping the thermostat at a moderate temperature, therefore, can help reduce unnecessary energy use.
Setting the air conditioner to 18°C may seem like an effective way to cool a room quickly, but it can significantly increase energy consumption. A setting of 24°C is generally sufficient to maintain a comfortable indoor environment during hot weather.
Instead of lowering the temperature excessively, gradually adjust your nighttime settings to 24°C. This can help maintain comfort while reducing the strain on the air conditioner's cooling system.
An air conditioner works more efficiently when cool air remains inside the room. Open doors, poorly sealed windows, and gaps around frames allow cool air to escape while letting warm air enter.
Make sure all doors and windows are properly closed before switching on the AC. Check for gaps that may need sealing and use curtains to reduce heat entering through windows.
Electronic appliances generate heat while operating, which can increase the cooling load on an air conditioner. Televisions, computers, and other devices can contribute to indoor heat, making the AC work harder to maintain the desired temperature.
Switch off appliances that are not in use before going to bed. This can help reduce unnecessary heat generation and improve cooling efficiency.
Running an air conditioner throughout the night may not always be necessary. As the room cools down, maintaining the same level of cooling until morning can lead to unnecessary electricity consumption.
Use the timer function to schedule the AC to switch off one or two hours before your usual wake-up time, if the room remains comfortable. This can help avoid excessive cooling and reduce operating time.
With the right temperature settings, proper room insulation, and mindful use of household appliances, you can enjoy a cooler night's sleep without putting unnecessary pressure on your electricity bill.

Hakimi bags hat-trick as PSG rip Le Havre to pieces
item.description:
Achraf Hakimi rose to the occasion scoring a glorious hat-trick on Friday as a heavily rotated Paris Saint-Germain thumped rock-bottom Le Havre 5-1 in Ligue 1.
PSG's nearest Ligue 1 rivals Rennes lost 5-2 at Nice dropping four points adrift while Olivier Giroud's late goal lifted Lille second after their 1-0 home win over Lens.
The former World Cup and Champions League winner Giroud is now 40 and the giant striker was flushed red with pleasure after his 86th minute shot settled a tense, tight struggle.
PSG top the table with 20 points after nine games, Lille are second on 18, Monaco can join them should they beat Paris FC on Sunday, while Rennes have 16.
On just two points so far Le Havre gave PSG a game early on as they suddenly surged forward in numbers with the PSG backline scampering in retreat before striker Josh Maja hammered in the opener against the run of play on 18 minutes.
Pushing for a second, Le Havre were carved open in a quick-fire move with Belgian winger Mika Godts racing onto a Hakimi through-ball to level on 26 minutes.
Two minutes later Hakimi left the defence trailing and his blistering low drive just inside the near post made it 2-1.
The European champions were running the Normandy side ragged before Hakimi scored his second with a fierce free-kick that curled low past the 'keeper Arnaud Bodard to put PSG 3-1 up.
On a lightning break the hosts poured everyone forward in a brave but naive effort to get back into the game, only for PSG to burst back, catching the home goalkeeper way off his line with not a single defender in his half.
Senny Mayulu ran around the horrified stopper, and his cool long-range finish hit the back of the net with nobody in the box effectively ending the contest, just after the hour.
Hakimi's hat-trick arrived when he threaded a shot through a forest of players on 69 minutes and had hardly finished a triumphant celebration when coach Luis Enrique subbed him off.
"He's a striker when we have the ball. He's free to do that when we are in possession, but obliged to defend when we aren't," said Luis Enrique.
The Spanish coach left stars Desire Doue, Vitinha and Joao Neves on the bench while Ousmane Dembele and Georgian attacker Khvicha Kvaratskhelia were missing through injury.

item.title: Dengue: 3 more die, 1,262 hospitalized in 24hrs
item.description:
Three people died of dengue in the last 24 hours till 8am on Friday, while 1,262 were hospitalized after being infected with the mosquito-borne disease during the same period.
The latest fatalities have raised the country's dengue death toll to 418 this year, according to the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
Of the newly-hospitalized dengue patients, 435 were in Dhaka Division, 75 in Mymensingh Division, 268 in Chittagong Division, 131 in Khulna Division, 112 in Rajshahi Division, 48 in Rangpur Division, 182 in Barisal Division and 11 in Sylhet Division.
According to the report, a total of 133,367 dengue patients have, so far, been hospitalized across the country this year.
So far, 126,713 dengue patients have recovered and returned home after receiving treatment in the hospitals.
A total of 102,861 people were infected with dengue, and 413 people died from the mosquito- borne disease last year.

item.title: Measles outbreak: Death toll reaches 1,251 as two die in 24 hours
item.description:
Two more children died with measles symptoms in the past 24 hours, starting at 8am on Thursday.
Besides, 1,391 suspected and confirmed measles cases were reported during the same period, a press release issued by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) said here on Friday.
With two deaths, the total number of fatalities from the suspected measles reached 1,146 since March 15, 2026, the release said.
"No one died from confirmed measles in the last 24 hours," it said, adding that a total of 105 children have died from confirmed measles since March 15.
The total number of fatalities from confirmed measles and measles-like symptoms has reached 1,251 so far, since March 15.
According to the release, 1,316 suspected measles cases were reported in the last 24 hours, while the number of suspected cases stood at 227,673 from March 15 to October 30.
Since March 15, the number of confirmed measles cases was 75 in the last 24 hours, bringing the total number of confirmed cases to 23,770.
A total of 202,639 patients with suspected measles were admitted to different hospitals across the country from March 15 to October 30. A total of 194,399 patients were discharged from the hospitals during the period.

item.title: Bangladesh, Japan stress stronger economic ties, alternative financing
item.description:
Bangladesh and Japan on Friday, underscored the need to strengthen their longstanding economic relations and expand cooperation in alternative financing to accelerate infrastructure development and deepen bilateral economic partnership.
The issue came up at a bilateral meeting between Finance Minister Amir Khosru Mahmud Chowdhury and his Japanese counterpart Satsuki Katayama at the Japanese Finance Minister’s office in Tokyo, according to a finance ministry media release received on Friday.
Japanese Assistant Finance Minister Mimura Atsushi also attended the meeting, which took place in a cordial atmosphere.
During the meeting, the two sides recalled the longstanding and strong economic relations between Bangladesh and Japan and held detailed discussions on ways to take their bilateral and economic partnership to a new height, said the release.
They put special emphasis on expanding economic cooperation through alternative financing mechanisms beyond foreign direct investment (FDI), alongside infrastructure development and trade expansion.
Both sides expressed their agreement to take effective initiatives to make the existing economic partnership more dynamic and explore opportunities for cooperation in new sectors. Special Assistant to the prime minister on Investment and Capital Market Affairs Tanvir Ghani and senior officials from both countries were also present at the meeting.
Japan remains one of Bangladesh’s major development partners. Japanese financing has supported several large-scale infrastructure and social development projects in Bangladesh in the past, while the two countries continue to implement important projects and sign new agreements.

item.title: CHT minister for building drug and unemployment-free Bandarban
item.description:
Chittagong Hill Tracts (CHT) Affairs Minister Sa Ching Prue on Friday expressed his determination to ensure balanced development of the CHT, create employment and build an unemployment-free Bandarban.
At the same time, he called upon leaders and activists of Jubo Dal to remain united to build a drug-free Bangladesh and a drug-free Bandarban hill district.
The minister said this while addressing a youth rally as the chief guest at the Press Club premises, held after a rally organised by the Bandarban District Jubo Dal to mark the 48th founding anniversary of Bangladesh Jatiyatabadi Jubo Dal, according to a PID release.
He said the harmful impact of drugs is increasing day by day everywhere in the country and drugs have now become a national problem. Although Cox's Bazar has been identified as the main route of drugs, its serious impact is being seen in the CHT, including Naikhongchhari, Alikadam and Thanchi, he said.
Outlining the future development plans for Bandarban, the minister said balanced development of the CHT must be ensured without being driven by emotion, by keeping the bonds of amity and harmony strong.
He said extensive employment opportunities will be created in Bandarban by taking everyone along, irrespective of party and opinion.
"By adopting specific and coordinated plans, we want to build a completely unemployment-free Bandarban," he said.
Bandarban District Jubo Dal President Zahir Uddin Masum presided over the rally, while the district Jubo Dal General Secretary Md Ariful Islam Chowdhury moderated it.
A large number of leaders and activists of the Bandarban unit of the Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) and its various associate organisations were present at the programme.

item.title: Tuku: Govt working to ensure healthcare services for disadvantaged people
item.description:
State Minister for Fisheries and Livestock Sultan Salahuddin Tuku has said the government is prioritising efforts to ensure healthcare assistance and development programmes reach disadvantaged people at the grassroots level.
He said Prime Minister Tarique Rahman has placed particular emphasis on supporting underprivileged people, especially those suffering from cancer, kidney disease and other critical illnesses, by providing financial assistance for their treatment.
Tuku made the remarks on Friday afternoon while distributing cheques among poor patients suffering from cancer, kidney disease and other complex illnesses at the Tangail Sadar Upazila Parishad building.
He said anyone suffering from a serious illness who had not yet received medical assistance could apply for support, pledging to take all possible steps to help them. “The programme will continue. We are committed to the people and will continue working for their welfare,” he said.
The state minister added that the scope of government assistance had expanded across various sectors since the BNP assumed office. Initiatives include family cards, farmer cards and allowances for imams and muezzins, alongside development activities across the country.
He said the government was taking all possible measures to ensure that public services and assistance reached people at the grassroots level.
At the programme, six patients each received Tk100,000, bringing the total amount distributed to Tk600,000.
Tangail Sadar Upazila Nirbahi Officer Shaheen Mia chaired the event. Among those present were former Tangail district BNP general secretary Mahmudul Haque Sanu, Tangail Sadar Thana BNP President Azgar Ali, former district BNP organising secretaries Ashraf Paheli and Shafiqul Rahman Shafik, and Tangail district Jubo Dal Convener Khandaker Rashedul Alam Rashed.
Union parishad chairmen, leaders and activists of the BNP and its affiliated organisations, and local dignitaries also attended.
After the cheque distribution, Tuku inaugurated a visitors' room at his office as part of efforts to improve public access to services and make government activities more accessible.

item.title: Biman forms probe body over technical glitch on PM's flight
item.description:
Biman Bangladesh Airlines has formed an investigation committee to determine the cause of a technical malfunction that delayed a flight carrying Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and his entourage in Japan.
Shahnur Ahmed, general manager of Biman's public relations department, confirmed the development to Dhaka Tribune on Friday.
He said the airline had formed an internal committee under its standard procedure for investigating such incidents and instructed it to submit its findings promptly.
The committee will be headed by Biman's Chief of Planning and Scheduling. Its members include the chief engineer (Engineering Production), deputy chief (Flight Safety) and manager (Legal Affairs), who will serve as member secretary.
The committee has been tasked with identifying the cause and nature of the malfunction, reviewing the measures taken to ensure the aircraft's airworthiness, and assessing the impact on flight schedules, passengers and the airline's reputation.
It will submit its report to Biman's managing director and chief executive officer.
Flight BG377, carrying the prime minister and his entourage, departed Narita International Airport in Japan five and a half hours behind schedule due to the technical glitch.
Biman's engineering team and Japanese technicians completed the repairs. The aircraft was pushed back at 7:43pm Bangladesh time and departed for Dhaka at 7:55pm.
